ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$, where $AB=6$, $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and $F$ is a point on side $CD$. The triangle $CEF$ is folded along $EF$ to obtain the triangle $GEF$. Connect $CG$ and extend it to intersect $EF$ and $AB$ at points $O$ and $H$, respectively. If $G$ is the midpoint of $OH$, what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
it follows that $\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
since $AB=6$ and E is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
then $CE=BE=\frac{1}{2}AB=3$,\\
since $\triangle CEF$ is folded along $EF$ to obtain $\triangle GEF$,\\
it follows that $EF$ bisects $CG$ perpendicularly,\\
thus $OG=OC$, $\angle COE=90^\circ$\\
Given G is the midpoint of $OH$,\\
then $OG=GH$,\\
therefore $OG=GH=OC=\frac{1}{3}CH$,\\
let $OC=x$, then $CH=3x$,\\
since $\angle COE=\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle OCE=\angle BCH$,\\
it follows that $\triangle COE\sim \triangle CBH$,\\
which means $\frac{CO}{BC}=\frac{CE}{CH}$,\\
thus $\frac{x}{6}=\frac{3}{3x}$,\\
solving gives $x=\sqrt{6}$,\\
therefore $CO=\sqrt{6}$,\\
hence $OE=\sqrt{CE^2-CO^2}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
therefore $\sin\angle OCE=\frac{OE}{CE}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
since $\angle CFO+\angle OCF=\angle OCE+\angle OCF=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CFO=\angle OCE$,\\
thus $\sin\angle CFO=\sin\angle OCE=\frac{OC}{CF}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
hence $CF=\sqrt{3}OC=\sqrt{3}\times \sqrt{6}=\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$

By the folding relation, triangle CEF is folded along EF to triangle GEF, so C and G are symmetric with respect to EF, so EF is the perpendicular bisector of CG. Thus O is the midpoint of CG, CO=OG, and CO⊥EF. Also because G is the midpoint of OH, OG=GH. Along the straight line C-O-G-H there is CO=OG=GH; let CO=x, then CH=CO+OG+GH=3x. The corresponding side ratio is CO/BC=CE/CH, that is x/6=3/(3x). Solving gives x²=6, so CO=√6. In right triangle COE, CE=3 and CO=√6, so OE=√(CE²-CO²)=√(9-6)=√3. Therefore sin∠OCE=OE/CE=√3/3. Also because EF⊥CG, FO⊥CO; meanwhile CF⊥CE. Thus ∠CFO and ∠OCE are both complementary to ∠OCF, so ∠CFO=∠OCE. In right triangle CFO, sin∠CFO=CO/CF. Therefore CO/CF=√3/3; substituting CO=√6 gives CF=√3·√6=√18=3√2. Final answer: CF=3√2.

method.method_draft: Synthetic similarity and angle-chasing route. First read the diagram as a square with A bottom-left, B bottom-right, C top-right, D top-left; E lies on BC, F lies on CD, and the line CG passes through O on EF, then G, then H on AB. From the text, AB=BC=6 and E is the midpoint of BC, so CE=3. Use the right angles at O and B and the shared angle along CH to prove triangles COE and CBH are similar. Then x/6=3/(3x), so x=sqrt(6). In right triangle COE, compute OE=sqrt(CE^2-CO^2)=sqrt(3). Finally use the fact that EF is perpendicular CG while CF is perpendicular CE, giving the complementary-angle relation angle CFO=angle OCE. Thus sin(angle CFO)=sin(angle OCE)=OE/CE=sqrt(3)/3, but in right triangle CFO, sin(angle CFO)=CO/CF. Hence CF=sqrt(3)CO=3sqrt(2).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个正方形 ABCD，A 在左下，B 在右下，C 在右上，D 在左上。点 E 在右边 BC 上，位置为中点附近；点 F 在上边 CD 上。线段 EF 从 F 连到 E，线段 CG 从 C 经过 EF 上的交点 O，再经过内部点 G，延长到下边 AB 上的点 H。图中还画出了 FG 和 GE，表示折叠后得到的三角形 GEF。

推理：因为 ABCD 是正方形且 AB=6，所以 BC=6，且 CE=BE=3。由折叠关系，三角形 CEF 沿 EF 折到三角形 GEF，因此 C 与 G 关于 EF 对称，所以 EF 是 CG 的垂直平分线。于是 O 是 CG 的中点，CO=OG，并且 CO⊥EF。又因为 G 是 OH 的中点，所以 OG=GH。沿直线 C-O-G-H 有 CO=OG=GH，设 CO=x，则 CH=CO+OG+GH=3x。

因为 CO⊥OE，所以 ∠COE=90°；正方形中 ∠CBH=90°。又 O、G、H、C 共线，且 E、C、B 共线，所以 ∠OCE=∠BCH。因此 △COE∼△CBH。对应边比例为 CO/BC=CE/CH，即 x/6=3/(3x)。解得 x²=6，所以 CO=√6。

在直角三角形 COE 中，CE=3，CO=√6，所以 OE=√(CE²-CO²)=√(9-6)=√3。因此 sin∠OCE=OE/CE=√3/3。

又因为 EF⊥CG，所以 FO⊥CO；同时 CF⊥CE。于是 ∠CFO 与 ∠OCE 都和 ∠OCF 互余，所以 ∠CFO=∠OCE。在直角三角形 CFO 中，sin∠CFO=CO/CF。因此 CO/CF=√3/3，代入 CO=√6，得到 CF=√3·√6=√18=3√2。

最终答案：CF=3√2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the square $ABCD$, where $AB=6$, $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and $F$ is a point on side $CD$. The triangle $CEF$ is folded along $EF$ to obtain the triangle $GEF$. Connect $CG$ and extend it to intersect $EF$ and $AB$ at points $O$ and $H$, respectively. If $G$ is the midpoint of $OH$, what is the length of $CF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square,\\
it follows that $\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
since $AB=6$ and E is the midpoint of $BC$,\\
then $CE=BE=\frac{1}{2}AB=3$,\\
since $\triangle CEF$ is folded along $EF$ to obtain $\triangle GEF$,\\
it follows that $EF$ bisects $CG$ perpendicularly,\\
thus $OG=OC$, $\angle COE=90^\circ$\\
Given G is the midpoint of $OH$,\\
then $OG=GH$,\\
therefore $OG=GH=OC=\frac{1}{3}CH$,\\
let $OC=x$, then $CH=3x$,\\
since $\angle COE=\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle OCE=\angle BCH$,\\
it follows that $\triangle COE\sim \triangle CBH$,\\
which means $\frac{CO}{BC}=\frac{CE}{CH}$,\\
thus $\frac{x}{6}=\frac{3}{3x}$,\\
solving gives $x=\sqrt{6}$,\\
therefore $CO=\sqrt{6}$,\\
hence $OE=\sqrt{CE^2-CO^2}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
therefore $\sin\angle OCE=\frac{OE}{CE}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
since $\angle CFO+\angle OCF=\angle OCE+\angle OCF=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CFO=\angle OCE$,\\
thus $\sin\angle CFO=\sin\angle OCE=\frac{OC}{CF}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
hence $CF=\sqrt{3}OC=\sqrt{3}\times \sqrt{6}=\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$

Segment EF connects from F to E, and segment CG goes from C through the intersection point O on EF, then through the interior point G, and is extended to point H on the lower side AB.
